sections.history: Tiruppenuperundurai lies near Nachiyarkoil, on the southern bank of the Arisilar river, about 10–12 km from Kumbakonam, in Thanjavur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, and counted the 64th shrine on the southern bank of the Kaveri. Its historical name, Tiruppenuperundurai, distinguishes it from the Tirupperundurai bound to Manickavasagar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Sivanandeswarar — also Pranaveswarar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Mangalambikai (also Malayarasi Ammai) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the Vanni tree and the temple tank is the Mangala Theertham. The walled courtyard keeps the form of the Shiva temples of the Kumbakonam country.
sections.legends: Shiva is worshipped here as Sivanandeswarar, 'the lord of the bliss of Shiva,' and as Pranaveswarar, the lord of the Om; the goddess is Mangalambikai, 'the auspicious mother,' also praised as Malayarasi Ammai. As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and Sambandar's verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims of the Kumbakonam country include Tiruppenuperundurai among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tiruppenuperundurai the pilgrim comes to the lord of Shiva's bliss by the Arisilar. Before Sivanandeswarar and Mangalambikai, under the Vanni tree, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple of the Kumbakonam delta.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruppenuperundurai lies near Nachiyarkoil, on the southern bank of the Arisilar, about 10–12 km from Kumbakonam, in Thanjavur district. Kumbakonam is the nearest town and rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
